evidence_quotes.quote: CONTRIBUTION TO THE STUDY OF MEASURES FOR THE REDUCTION OF APPARENT WATER LOSS IN URBAN AREAS
in this study was evaluated the influence of metrological class and the usage time of meters on under-registration, through study on pilot scale and tests in a laboratory scale.
Furthermore, discoursed out about the interference of the use of water tanks and about the influence of tariff policy on the financial performance of the utilities and consumption of users.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: No divergence between narrow and plain Criterion 2 decisions: both exclude the record because the empirical investigation is a laboratory- and pilot-scale engineering/metrological test of water meter under-registration and utility apparent water losses, while tariff policy is only discussed regarding utility financial performance and user consumption rather than empirically analysed as a determinant of household service access.
raw_response.rationale: This study is an engineering/metrological evaluation (pilot-scale and laboratory-scale testing) of water meter classes (Class B vs. Class C) and meter usage time to reduce meter under-registration and utility apparent water/revenue losses, together with a cost-benefit assessment for the utility. Although the paper also discusses household water tanks and the influence of tariff policy on utility financial performance and user water consumption, it neither empirically examines a legal/administrative mechanism governing household service access nor measures household water access, connection, reliability, affordability, or exclusion outcomes (primary exclusion: E06 engineering only).
